definition: A normalization technique that normalizes activations across the features of a single training example rather than across a batch.
details: Layer normalization is widely used in transformer architectures because it works well with variable sequence lengths and small batch sizes, unlike batch normalization.

explainer.lead: Layer normalization normalizes the activations of each training example across its features, independent of other examples in the batch. It is a standard ingredient in transformer architectures.

tiers.eli5: Each example gets its own ruler to measure and rescale its numbers, so it does not matter who else is in the group.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on it when batch sizes are small or sequence lengths vary; a pitfall is assuming it substitutes for batch normalization everywhere, since behaviour differs across architectures.
tiers.paperLevel: For a single example, activations are normalized across features, usually with learned scale and shift; unlike batch normalization it uses no cross-example statistics.

explainer.example: A transformer block normalizes each token's hidden vector across its feature dimension before the attention sublayer.
